Done. `docs/2026-08-02_results_narrative_final_order_D.md` has the two sections as continuous prose, the corrections, the dose list, both questions answered with citations, and the panel table. Committed `b0feba3`, not pushed.

**Your timeline vs A/B/C.** It is **C's skeleton with B's hinge** — the recommendation, arrived at independently — plus two improvements that are yours: apoptosis moves *into* section 1 (so "competent but not more primed" is established before the window argument needs it), and the questions are explicit at the end rather than buried. I've called it Order D and the A/B/C doc stays as the record.

**Three things in your spine the data changed.** Two of them help.

1. **PUMA is not deprioritised in the background.** `Bbc3` in WT 6→12W is **+0.06, padj 0.88 — flat**. It falls only in Myc+ (−0.48, padj 0.016), interaction p = 0.0081. So "OXPHOS and PUMA are deprioritised" splits: **OXPHOS is the Myc-independent half, PUMA is the Myc-dependent half.** That is your two-input model stated exactly, and it turns the hand-off into a real prediction rather than a restatement.
2. **The background is not the mirror of Myc's reprioritisation** — r = −0.02 across 143 pathways, 50% sign-discordant. *Independent*, not opposite. The flips on OXPHOS/import/apoptosis are real but picking those four is selection unless a null is quoted, and only the content ruler has one (subunits 0th percentile, assembly factors 50th).
3. **"Favours OXPHOS" holds at tier level, not leaf level** — the biggest promotions are one-carbon/amino-acid (glycine cleavage +0.41, creatine +0.37, pyruvate +0.33), and it is the **subunits, not the assembly factors** (−0.028). That same subunit-vs-assembly split reappears in the WT withdrawal, so one sub-compartment carries both halves of the paper.

**Six things you'd left out**, chief among them: mitochondrial **content +21–27%** (without it a reader takes "reprioritisation" for a content claim); Myc's **repressive arm fades faster** than its inductive arm (0.33 vs 0.51); and the single largest departure from the dose line in the transcriptome is the **release of luminal suppression** (`MG_HS_GRAY` −0.47 → +0.09, padj 1.7e-17) — flagged, not placed, since Fig. 1B owns de-differentiation.

**Your two questions.**

*Foxo3?* — **Yes, and the answer was already on disk.** In the departure-from-dose scan over 8,774 genes, `Foxo3` sits at the **0.456th percentile** and `Bbc3` at the **0.513th** — adjacent, interaction p 0.0074 and 0.0081, the two lowest in the rosters. Direction is the tell: **WT raises Foxo3 with age (+0.47, padj 0.0078), Myc+ does not.** Both hold position within the Myc-induced genes alone, so neither rides the repressive-arm asymmetry. FOXO3 is AKT-regulated post-translationally — which is why the western you already have queued is the test.

*PUMA/MPC?* — Your memory is right and the naive arrow does fail. PUMA disrupts MPC1–MPC2 oligomerisation ([Kim, *Cancer Cell* 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1535610818305841)), so PUMA down should raise OXPHOS. But our MPC tracks *Myc*, not inverse-PUMA (`Mpc2` +0.69 padj 0.0084, falling with age in Myc+). So respiration is **upstream**: cells without OXPHOS and with low Δψm are *less* killable ([Dey & Moraes, *JBC* 2000](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021925818303995)), and FOXO3 transactivates *BBC3* directly ([Fitzwalter, *Dev Cell* 2018](https://www.cell.com/developmental-cell/fulltext/S1534-5807(18)30109-6)). The circuit that reconciles both is negative feedback — respiration → FOXO3 → PUMA → MOMP, with PUMA braking the state that induced it — under which the co-decline is *expected* and PGC-1a should restore both.

*Why not the interaction?* — Both halves of your instinct. Power: median lfcSE **0.333 vs 0.233** (the √2 of a difference-of-differences) on a *smaller* effect, so ~3× the detectable threshold. And the null is wrong: under a global rescaling every Myc-responsive gene has a non-zero interaction by construction. And **the non-linearity has a published mechanism** — affinity-ordered promoter occupancy ([Lorenzin, *eLife* 2016](https://elifesciences.org/articles/15161)), with our retentions ordering exactly as predicted: core 0.74–0.77 > global 0.55 > mito arms 0.50–0.58 >> PUMA −0.09. Affinity explains everything above the line and cannot make a sign reversal — which is what makes PUMA the residual worth an experiment.

**Panels** are commissioned in `PANELS.md` as Fig. 2A–2D (oncogene) and 3A–3D (tissue). Seven of the eight are **ports** of `figures/fig01`–`fig05`/`figS8` into the panel idiom; only **3C** (the departure-from-dose distribution with Foxo3 and Bbc3 marked, Bax and Bcl2l11 as controls) is new. Fig. 1E is recorded as superseded.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Two rulers.** Content (raw set-mean LFC, dose-dominated) vs mitoPPS *priority* (pairwise ratio within the mitochondrial compartment, content-blind — a uniform scaling cancels).
   - **Rescaled not reshaped.** `Myc@12W = 0.552 × Myc@6W`, intercept 0, R² 0.80 over 143 mito pathways; priority slope 0.644 R² 0.789; OXPHOS priority R² 0.945; R² at the 100th percentile of matched nulls.
   - **Dose vs competence.** MMTV-Myc 6→12W is a *dose* experiment (MYC protein −50% at constant transcript ⇒ ×0.55); MYC-ER is a *competence* experiment (~80% less death vs ~30% less proliferation, animals never previously exposed).
   - **Departure-from-dose scan** (script 44): `resid_aligned = sign(LFC6) * (LFC12 - RATE * LFC6)`, `RATE` assumed 0.55 / fitted 0.487; negative aligned residual = collapse past the line regardless of the 6W direction.
   - **Affinity-ordered E-box occupancy** (Lorenzin *eLife* 2016) as the published mechanism for non-linear de-dosing.
   - **The interaction is under-powered *and* mis-specified**: SE 0.333 vs 0.233 on a smaller effect; and under a global rescaling every Myc-responsive gene has a non-zero interaction by construction, so testing against zero is the wrong null.
   - **`batch = timepoint`** — WT temporal statements are described, not claimed; blots are the off-batch mitigation.
   - **Epistemic contract** — the mouse supplies contrast; the perturbations supply causality. Priming ≠ death.

**The one design choice worth checking.** The number your sentence quotes is the *pooled* genotype effect, so the groups are drawn **genotype-major** (both WT boxes, then both Myc+) and one bracket spans the two halves — that bracket *is* `lm(log2 share ~ timepoint + myc_status)`, reproduced from script 32 to 1e-8. This is the opposite order from `figS1_mb_fork_specificity.R`, which is age-major because its test is within an age. The order follows the test.

## Three things in the paragraph that need a word changed

- **"94% of 143"** mixes two numbers — 94.4 % is over all **144** ruler rows, 95.1 % over the **143** the fits and the panel use.
- **"21–27%"** is narrower than what the panel shows. Those are the median per-gene rise (+21.4 %) and the mass markers (+26.5 %); the five *set* arms run **+20 % to +33 %**.
- **"(padj < 0.001)" is the pooled effect.** Split by age at n = 6/cell it clears 0.05 at **12W** on all four nuclear arms and only on biogenesis at **6W** (0.034; the rest 0.08–0.11). The effect size is the same at both ages — every interaction p is 0.35–0.81 — so pooling is right, but the sentence shouldn't imply a six-week significance the six-week data alone don't carry.

Three more, for later paragraphs: complex IV is **flat** on the priority ruler (+0.017; CV and CIII carry the tier, and the assembly factors sit at −0.028), so "all complexes" wants softening; `Bbc3`'s "(p < 0.01)" is 0.0081 with BH 0.84, licensed by pre-specification, which the text doesn't yet say; and Fig. 1G's `R2=***` placeholders have candidates but the "whole transcriptome" one needs picking. All six are in PANELS.md.

**Fig. 1G is built** (`486d5a0`). 89 × 62 mm — two scatters over the null.

```
source(here::here("figures", "panels", "fig1_rescaled_not_reshaped.R"))   # print(p); print(LEGEND)
```

The panel separates two things your sentence runs together. **"Half amplitude" is the slope; "unchanged in shape" is the R².** They are independent, and only one is beyond its null:

| | observed | null median | null max | draws ≥ obs | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| slope | 0.552 | 0.419 | — | **64 of 500** | 0.13 |
| **R²** | **0.801** | 0.298 | **0.719** | **0 of 500** | **< 0.002** |

A shuffled set of the same size and expression *can* halve an effect. What it cannot do is halve it coherently. So the null strip sits under the scatter rather than in the text — and **the `p<` in your parenthesis attaches to the R², not to the slope.**

## Your `R2=***` placeholders

| | number |
|---|---|
| whole transcriptome, slope | **0.487** (through origin, the 2,648 genes Myc moves — script 44's rate of record, asserted) |
| whole transcriptome, "overall R2" | **0.51** — *or* 0.450 / **0.381** over all 8,774 reported genes |
| mitochondrial, slope | **0.552**, intercept 0.0001 (a pure rescaling, not a shift), boot 0.514–0.605 |
| mitochondrial, "overall R2" | **0.801** |
| **"OXPHOS R2"** | **0.761** — content ruler. **Not 0.945**: that is the *priority* ruler and belongs with your "see Fig. 1F" clause, not inside the same parenthesis |
| "p <" | **0.002** |

**One word needed on "whole transcriptome."** The left facet is labelled *Myc-responsive genes (2,648)* because that is the set 0.487 is fitted on. Over all 8,774 the slope barely moves (0.450) but R² falls to 0.381 — regression dilution from the six thousand genes Myc doesn't move. Either pair is fine; they mustn't be crossed.

Also: R² is the squared Pearson correlation in both facets, so they use one definition. A through-origin `lm` reports an *uncentred* R² (0.565 not 0.513) that isn't comparable to the pathway facet — don't quote that one.

**Next: Fig. 1H** — "not just maintained but enhanced: the NES for the mitochondrial OXPHOS set and MYC integrative signatures increased substantially." That's the first genuinely new build (no port), and Fig. 1D already draws both genotype contrasts by programme, so 1H needs to be the set-level view: NES at 12W against NES at 6W over the 866 ranked sets, with the named ones marked.

**Fig. 1H is built** (`ca948f8`), 89 × 62 mm — but it does not support the sentence as written, and you should see why before deciding what to do.

```
source(here::here("figures", "panels", "fig1_nes_preserved_sharpened.R"))   # print(p); print(LEGEND)
```

866 sets, NES at 12W against NES at 6W, identity line, OXPHOS and Myc signatures picked out by the same `programme_group()` Fig. 1D uses for its rows.

## "Maintained" is true — and stronger than you wrote it

**Spearman 0.933** while the effect size halves. Better: the **92 sets that cross sign** between the ages — the two off-diagonal clouds — are **84 % mammary-development and TF-target sets**. Set them aside and Spearman over the remaining 774 is **0.967**. *What holds its order is the metabolic/mitochondrial/Myc core; what reshuffles is lineage identity* — section 2's subject, arriving early.

## "Enhanced" does not survive, on two counts

**1. The rise is not specific — every point is above the line.** 81 % of all 866 sets rise (median +0.312); 93 % of the 403 already enriched at 6W (median +0.319). As *families*, the two you name rise by **the median amount**: OXPHOS +0.308 = **49th percentile**, Myc signatures +0.386 = **60th**. The numbers in the Order D doc (MITOCARTA_OXPHOS +0.52, MYC_felsher +0.55) are the best members of those families, at the 76th/78th percentile — upper quartile, not exceptional.

**2. A global NES rise is what a weaker ranking mechanically produces.** fGSEA normalises each enrichment score against a permutation null built from *that same ranked list*. The 12W Wald list is much flatter — **SD 1.22 vs 1.74, IQR 1.50 vs 2.18, 9.5 % of genes past |stat| = 2 vs 22.5 %** — so random sets reach smaller scores, the normaliser shrinks, and identical relative enrichment scores higher. No claim of increased Myc activity can rest on NES.

## The sentence I'd write instead

NES is enrichment *relative to the rest of the transcriptome*, so what the panel does say is that these programmes **hold their position at the top of the ranking while the amplitude halves** — the residual Myc signal is more concentrated on them than it was. That is the retention asymmetry (Myc core 0.74–0.77 vs the mitochondrial arms' 0.50–0.58) on a different instrument. **Position, not magnitude** — which sits *beside* 1G rather than in tension with it.

Also visible and still unplaced: the upper-left cloud is the release of Myc's suppression of luminal hormone-sensing identity (`MG_LHS_CONSENSUS` −3.20 → +2.05), the largest single departure from the dose line in the transcriptome.

Figure 1's R panels are done: **1B–1H**. Next is **Fig. S1E** (Myc transcript stable), then S1F.

**Fig. S1E is built** (`6ca14cb`). 55 × 55 mm.

```
source(here::here("figures", "panels", "figS1_myc_transcript_stable.R"))   # print(p); print(LEGEND)
```

Myc transcript, four groups, every animal. The genotype gap is **+1.68 → +1.82** and the Myc+ gland does not decline (**−0.10, padj 0.76**) — so the blot's halving is not the transgene being silenced. `Myc` is the single most retained gene in the transcriptome (retention 1.085, 99.99th percentile of 8,774).

Three choices worth knowing:

- **Age-major group order**, the opposite of 1E — because the order follows the test. 1E draws one *pooled* genotype effect, so both WT boxes sit together under one bracket. Here the tests are the two *within-age* gaps, so each age's pair has to be adjacent.
- **y is log2 of normalised counts, labelled in counts**, so "the gap remained constant" is a constant vertical distance you can read off the page rather than take on trust.
- **The brackets carry DESeq2**, and the script asserts the drawn group means reproduce each fold change to within 0.1 — the picture and the statistic are the same quantity.

One wording item for the Doc: *"the expression gap remained constant **between 6W_myc and 12W_myc**"* — a gap is between genotypes, not between ages. Both readings are true here and the panel draws both, but the sentence should say which it means.

Also, `bracket_frame()` / `bracket_layers()` now live in `_panel_common.R` (the bar + end-ticks + label idiom), additive so it works on a log axis. S1F will use it too.

```
source(here::here("figures", "panels", "figS1_myc_network.R"))   # print(p); print(LEGEND)
```

Ten genes in three role blocks, each showing its Myc genotype effect at 6W and 12W joined, with ±1 SE on the 6W estimate. **Nothing clears padj 0.05 at either age** — closest are `Mxi1` (+0.33, padj 0.096) and `Mlx` (+0.39, padj 0.156) — and **no interaction is below padj 0.83**. So MAX doesn't fall and the repressors don't rise: the obvious alternative to a dose explanation is closed.

Three decisions:

- **It draws the contrast, not the level.** Your sentence claims the *gap*, so the gap is on the axis. The levels form (figS8 panel B) needs ten facets and 183 mm to say the same thing less directly.
- **No significance encoding**, because nothing is significant — a key whose "filled" entry never appears on the panel is worse than one sentence in the legend.
- **The error bar sits on the 6W point and is drawn over the connector in the 6W colour.** Underneath and in grey it read as spanning both points, which makes a 12W point falling outside it look like a real difference. One bar suffices because **the two ages are equally precise — SEs agree to within 0.024 log2 across all ten genes, median ratio 1.01** (asserted in the script). That's worth having on its own: *12W is not the noisier cohort*, which is the objection every attenuation result has to survive.

Also visible rather than assumed: `Mxd3` (baseMean 14, SE 0.52) and `Mlxipl` (baseMean 45, SE 0.33) are too lowly expressed to carry a negative — the bars show why.

**Figure 1 and Supplementary 1 are done** (1B–1H, S1A–S1C, S1E, S1F; S1D and 1A are yours). Next is **Fig. 2E** — the WT 6→12W transition: TEB lost, proliferation stable.

## The document

`outputs/figures/panels/Figure1_and_S1_panels.pdf` — **12 pages**, one panel each, in slot order (1B, 1C, 1D, 1E, 1F, 1G, 1H, S1A, S1B, S1C, S1E, S1F), the slot as the page title. Regenerate any time with:

```
source(here::here("figures", "panels", "panels_to_pdf.R"))
```

Two things worth knowing about it. It **re-renders from the scripts** rather than concatenating the existing PDFs — there is no Ghostscript, qpdf, pdftk, pdfjam or LaTeX on this machine and neither `qpdf` nor `pdftools` is installed, so nothing available could place one PDF page inside another; re-rendering also stays vector and can't go stale. And **each panel is drawn at its designed physical size** on a 105 × 111 mm page — scaling a ggplot to fill a page doesn't magnify it, it stretches the plot while the type stays at 6 pt, which would be a different picture from the one you signed off. Zoom does the magnifying. `legends.md` was refreshed alongside it, so all 13 legend blocks are current.

The MB-fork panel is left out: its legend block was still claiming `Fig. S1D`, which is now your blot, so I changed its slot to `not currently cited` and anything laying out by slot skips it.

   - **Tibble subsetting poisoned `sprintf`** — scripts 32/40/44 save tibbles; `stats[a, "n_genes"]` returned a 1×1 tibble, failing with "unsupported type" without naming the cause. Fixed by `as.data.frame()` on read everywhere; also `rownames(x) <-` on a tibble is deprecated.
   - **`sprintf` arg-count mismatch** ("%d of 143" hard-coded while passing `nrow(r143)`) — fixed to `%d of %d`.
   - **Clipped facet strip labels at 89 mm** — fixed with two-line arm names and `strip.clip = "off"`.
   - **p-value label sitting on its bracket bar** — fixed by adding a separate `y_lab` above the bar with `vjust = 0`.
   - **`SP` env var not visible to `Rscript`** — used the literal scratchpad path.
   - **`coord_cartesian` clipping impossible with `facet_wrap(scales = "free")`** — fixed by filtering the *drawn* points per facet and reporting the counts left out (22 genes, 2 pathways) in the legend.

   - **plotmath drops trailing zeros** — `R^2~0.80` parses as a number and prints `0.8`; fixed by quoting inside the string (`R^2~"0.80"`).
   - **`on.exit()` at the top level of a sourced script fires immediately** — it restored `myc.fig.capture` before any panel ran, so every panel wrote its own PDF instead of reporting its size. Fixed by removing all `on.exit()` from `panels_to_pdf.R` and restoring options/device explicitly.

| row | n | median NES | padj < 0.05 |
|---|---|---|---|
| TEB programmes | 38 | **−1.58** | **29**, and all 38 depleted |
| ductal (TEB-down) | 3 | **+1.06** | 1 |
| TEB × MitoCarta | 12 | +0.49 | 0 |
| proliferation | 14 | **−0.89** | **0** |

Shape is significance (Fig. 1F's encoding), the vertical rule is the family median, dashed guides at NES ±1 mark the scale of an unmoved set, and `MG_TEB_VS_DUCTAL_HS_GRAY_UP` (−2.76, p 3.4e−18) is labelled because it is the one set all three rulers share.

**One thing the first render caught.** The `_VS_DUCTAL_*_DN` sets were sitting inside the TEB row with their sign inverted by construction — they hold the genes *lower* in the end bud than in the duct. Pooling them cancelled part of the effect. On their own row they become the control your sentence actually needs: "lost as expected in the puberty-adult transition" is a directional claim, and a panel showing only sets going down could just be showing a ranking that drifts down. **They rise** — basal +1.45 against its UP set's −2.34, hormone-sensing +1.06 against −2.76 (alveolar shows neither, −1.13 vs −1.22, both n.s.).

**Three things for the text, all in the legend block and PANELS.md:**

1. **"Relatively stable" is right, with a qualifier.** Not one proliferation set is significant here — but on the gene-level ruler `PROLIF_*` pooled moves −0.047 log2 at the **1.3rd percentile** of its matched null (p = 0.013). *Small, not immobile.* The quantitative form: the TEB arm moves **8.9 times as far**.
2. **Three rulers agree on the TEB arm and two are composition-independent** — gene-level −0.4220 (0th percentile of 2000 matched sets) and the purity-adjusted per-sample composite −0.4200 (p 0.0053), agreeing to 0.002. Contamination does not explain the loss.
3. **The cell cycle really does not move — lineage does.** Generic E2F1 regulons are flat (DOROTHEA −1.18, ChIP-Atlas +0.86, both n.s.) while the Gray `_LE` lanes of the *same* transcription factors fall hard (FOXM1_HS_LE −2.10, TFDP1_HS_LE −2.08, E2F1_HS_LE −1.72, padj < 1e−3). Those are lineage-identity lanes. This is Fig. 1H's off-diagonal cloud arriving exactly where section 2 wants it.

Next in citation order is **Fig. 2F** — the respiratory withdrawal. Worth knowing before you look at it: on this same NES ruler, `MITOCARTA_OXPHOS_SUBUNITS` is **−2.67 (padj 1.3e−11)** while amino-acid **+1.84** and fatty-acid oxidation **+1.89** rise, and the assembly factors sit at **−0.74, n.s.** — your sentence's three clauses, on one instrument, with its own internal control.

Eleven MitoPathways ranked on the wild-type 6→12W contrast, drawn on **both rulers side by side** — content (set-average raw log2FC) and priority (mitoPPS, content-blind) — on separate scales, because they are separate units. Reading top to bottom:

| | content | priority |
|---|---|---|
| **CIV subunits** (17) | −0.411 | −0.180 |
| CI (36) / CIII (9) / CV (19) subunits | −0.253 / −0.251 / −0.216 | −0.155 / −0.126 / −0.069 |

| lipid (111), amino acid (79), FAO (39) | +0.122 … +0.227 | +0.063 … +0.144 |

**Both rulers are drawn because either alone is answerable** — a content drop could be normalisation, a content-blind ratio drop could be a reshuffle inside a growing compartment. Over all 143 non-mtDNA pathways they agree at **Spearman 0.82**.

**Two things came out of the data that strengthen your sentence:**

1. **The background is rising.** The median MitoPathway *gains* content over this window (+0.041, 72% above zero). So the respiratory arm isn't falling with the compartment — it's falling against it. That is what licenses "withdraw", and it's one clause.
2. **The assembly-factor control is doing more work than I expected.** They sit at +0.001, percentile **50.2** of the expression-matched null, where the pooled subunits sit at **0.0** — measured in the same libraries, on the same two batches. That's the strongest available answer to `batch = timepoint`, and it belongs in the text: *the gland withdraws the stoichiometry of the chain, not the machinery that builds it.*

**One wording item.** "Across all complexes" has an exception: **CII subunits rise** (+0.088 / +0.026) — the only complex with no mtDNA-encoded subunit and the only one outside the proton circuit. But n = 4, so it's a direction, not a mechanism. Suggested: *"across the four complexes that carry mtDNA-encoded subunits"*, or just name CI, CIII, CIV, CV.

**And one deliberate omission, flagged in the legend rather than hidden.** The 13 mtDNA-encoded subunits are excluded by the same `is_mtdna` rule as Figs. 1E/1F — and they are the largest movement in the compartment (**+0.633 content, +0.525 priority**). That's a nuclear-down/mtDNA-up discordance if real, but mt% is confounded three ways and is time-associated rather than genotype-associated, so the wild-type temporal contrast is precisely where it can't be read. The text shouldn't quote it either.

No significance is drawn because none exists for this contrast — script 40 saves adjusted p-values for the genotype contrasts only. What does exist is script 43's matched null, covering five of the eleven rows, and it's in the legend. Scripts 40 and 43 computed these arms independently; the script asserts they agree to 1e−6.

## Significance — yes, three kinds, and one of them I hadn't surfaced

2. **Per pathway, content ruler.** Nothing saved, and I deliberately didn't compute a one-sample t over member genes: that null ignores inter-gene correlation and would be anti-conservative for exactly the coherently-regulated sets this panel is about.
3. **Arm level, expression-matched null (2000 draws)** — decisive: OXPHOS subunits **percentile 0.0** (p < 0.0005) against their own assembly factors at **50.2**; amino-acid **100.0** and lipid **99.9** upward.

**The number to put in the sentence is one I hadn't given you: script 43's paired null.** "The chain falls *while* biogenesis does not" is a comparative claim, and script 43 tests it by redrawing *both* sets together — **OXPHOS subunits minus mitoribosome = −0.230, percentile 0.05, p = 0.0005** (minus nucleotide metabolism −0.255, p = 0.0085; minus the pooled proliferation set −0.208, p < 0.0005). That is the statistic for this sentence, and it's a stronger one than either arm alone.

Nothing is drawn, because a glyph would have to mark 8 tested pathways among 135 untested ones — which reads as 135 negatives. All of it is in the legend block.

Two things worth knowing about the build. **Labels are placed, not repelled** — ggrepel stacked the four knot labels on each other twice, so they go into two provably empty regions (upper-left, and the right band past +0.28), with the emptiness **re-derived from the data in a `stopifnot`** rather than trusted from the render, and lane order matched to the points' vertical order so no two leaders can cross. And the panel is **windowed** — two pathways sit below the priority range, both ≤5 genes. That's not incidental: **every point at the periphery of this cloud is a 3-to-6-gene set**, because a set mean's noise scales as 1/√n. The membership-loose caveat, made visible.

**Fig. S2B is built** — `figS2_reallocation_independence.R`, 89 × 52 mm, 16/16 panels rebuild, committed `68d45a6`.

Two scatters of the wild-type 6→12W change against the Myc effect at 6W: **143 MitoPathways on the priority ruler (r = −0.022)** and **15,191 genes on the log2 fold change (r = +0.228)**.

**The mitochondrial half is exactly as you wrote it. The whole-transcriptome half needed work, and the finding matters.**

`myc_6W` = 6W_myc − 6W_wt and `6>12W_wt` = 12W_wt − 6W_wt — **the same six wild-type animals are subtracted in both**, so a fluctuation in that baseline moves the two contrasts together and manufactures a positive correlation. Two independent estimates:

| | |
|---|---|
| observed | **+0.228** |
| predicted from the standard errors (Cov = Var(6W_wt) = SE²/2) | **+0.198** |
| **measured** — Myc effect against one half of the six animals, temporal effect against the other | **−0.025** |

So the sentence holds on both scopes: **−0.02 mitochondrial, −0.03 whole transcriptome**. The dashed line on the right-hand panel is what the tilt becomes once the baseline is broken; the solid line is the observed one.

Three things about the control worth knowing. It is **exhaustive, not sampled** — there are exactly `choose(6,3) = 20` assignments and all 20 are used, so the panel contains no RNG. It runs on VST rather than re-fitted DESeq2 models (re-fitting is an analysis, not a figure), and **what licenses that surrogate is asserted**: with the baseline shared, the VST version reproduces the drawn DESeq2 correlation to **0.002**. And splitting halves the baseline's n, which pulls |r| toward zero — undoing that inflation gives −0.032 rather than −0.025, so it doesn't turn on which you use.

The artefact also **pushes the wrong way for the mitochondrial panel**, which makes that negative conservative: the priority contrasts share the same baseline, so the sharing forces a *positive* correlation, and −0.02 is what we see.

Two things for the record, both in PANELS.md:

- **Cosine is not correlation here.** Script 40 reports the uncentred cosine (+0.210 on content); the correlation is −0.038. Both content vectors have a large positive mean and the cosine picks up that shared offset. The script asserts its recomputation matches `$geometry` exactly, so the panel provably draws script 40's vectors — but your sentence says *correlation*, so correlation is what is drawn. (Script 40's own null agrees: the cosine sits at the 41st percentile, i.e. at chance.)
- **This is not the claim that the Myc+ gland's own drift is independent of the wild-type one.** That regression has slope **0.749** — much of it *is* shared. Different pairs of vectors; they mustn't be run together in the text.

- **Script 34's circularity warning does not transfer here.** The PRO/ANTI sets are MitoCarta, so a *coupling* between priming and a mito axis is mito-vs-mito — but this is a temporal contrast on the transcripts themselves, correlated with nothing. Easy to import the caveat wrongly.

**Fig. 2G is built to the corrected sentence** — `fig2_priming_ratios.R`, 89 × 58 mm, 18/18 panels rebuild, committed `0c94f28`.

Your correction is the one the data support, and it made the panel simpler. It's **Fig. 1G's axes one level up**: the Myc effect on each pro-apoptotic:Bcl-xL log₂ ratio at 12W against 6W, with the **global rescaling rate 0.487** drawn as the *expected pattern* (labelled `x 0.49` on the page, since a bare line through a scatter reads as a regression and this one is imposed).

| ratio | 6W | 12W | retention | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Bax` | +0.901 | +0.495 | **0.55** | on the line |
| `Bid` | +0.946 | +0.396 | 0.42 | on the line |
| `Bak1` | +0.688 | +0.185 | 0.27 | a little under |
| **`Bbc3`** | **+0.674** | **−0.061** | **−0.09** | **crosses zero** |

**The members clause is exact, and it's in the legend:** `Bax` retains **0.52** of its 6W effect and `Bcl2l1` **0.57** — both at the global 0.49 — so their ratio retains 0.55. `Bbc3` retains **−1.10** against that same denominator. That is the whole of the difference, and it's why "remained stable" is the right verb for the others.

**One shared denominator is what makes the comparison internal** (script 42's own design note): BAX priming retains the global rate while PUMA priming reverses *against the same Bcl-xL*, so "it's just the global attenuation" is refuted from inside the panel.

**Shape is "established at 6W" and it's load-bearing, not decorative.** Retention is a quotient — for the three pairs whose 6W effect is indistinguishable from zero it carries no information (`Pmaip1`'s retention is +2.08 purely because its denominator is near zero). They're open circles with no residual drawn, and the four that are drawn are exactly the scope your sentence names.

**One item for the text: "significantly" needs its scope.** The interaction is **p = 0.037 raw, 0.017 purity-adjusted** — but **BH across the nine pairs is 0.33**, and against the matched-pair conditional null the **empirical p is 0.082**. It's a nominal result with a *pre-specified* licence (PUMA was named in advance from the PGC1a work), not a multiplicity-surviving one. The counterweight is in the legend too: on the empirical null the most extreme pair is `Bmf`, which Myc never established — which is exactly why the conditional null is the one to read.

And a caution worth carrying: the gene-level `Bbc3` interaction (**p = 0.0081**, which is 2H's subject) is a *different* statistic from this ratio interaction (**p = 0.037**). Easy to interchange.

**Fig. 2H is built** — `fig2_departure_from_dose.R`, 89 × 44 mm, 19/19 panels rebuild, committed `4a57c22`.

Script 44's per-gene departure from the dose expectation, drawn as the distribution over 8,774 genes with a rug of the bottom percentile:

| | z | genes below | percentile |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Foxo3` | **−2.53** | 39 of 8,774 | **0.46** |
| `Bbc3` | **−2.49** | 44 | **0.51** |
| `Bcl2l11` | +1.01 | 8,036 | 91.6 |

**"Closely tracking" has a sharp form, and the script asserts it: only four genes of 8,774 lie between them.** That's the number for the text.

**The panel carries the half that failed**, which is why `Bcl2l11` is marked. The scan was pre-registered with *two* genes and they split — `Bbc3` collapses, `Bcl2l11` sits in the ordinary middle at 91.6 with an interaction p of 0.86. Drawing only the gene that worked would be the wrong panel, so the key distinguishes **pre-specified** (filled) from **found in the scan** (open).

**And `Foxo3` was not pre-specified — it was found here.** Forty-four genes sit below the 0.5th percentile with it, mostly unrelated (`Adh7`, `Cntnap2`, `Inhba`, `Wfdc2`, `Vtcn1`…), so **position alone is not evidence**. What makes it a lead is the prior — FOXO3 is PUMA's canonical p53-independent activator with direct ChIP evidence. The text should introduce it that way round, and the legend says so.

Two things I've recorded that may be worth a clause each:

- **The same departure is reached by two different routes.** The wild-type gland *raises* `Foxo3` with age (+0.473) and the Myc+ gland does not (−0.013); `Bbc3`'s wild-type arm is flat (+0.062) while its Myc+ arm falls (−0.479). One is a failure to follow the normal developmental rise, the other an active loss.
- **The arrow is not the obvious one.** PUMA restrains the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (Kim, *Cancer Cell* 2019), so "PUMA falls → respiration falls" is backwards; respiration is upstream and FOXO3 → BBC3 closes it into feedback rather than a chain. Nothing on this panel establishes direction.

None of the interactions survives correction (`Bbc3` BH 0.84, `Foxo3` BH 1.00) — expected at n = 6 per cell, and why the licence is pre-specification rather than the p-value. A z of −2.5 among 8,774 genes is a rank statement, not a test.

Two remain: **S2D** (the other PUMA inducers) and **2I** (the OXPHOS × PUMA:Bcl-xL coupling).
